false_positives.evidence: name is inserted into uploads/ and out/ path fragments without basename validation or resolved-path containment checks.
false_positives.fix: Map an approved upload identifier to a server-owned filename, or resolve the path and verify it remains under fixed upload and output roots before processing.
false_positives.title: Image filename can escape application-controlled paths

trace.note: req.query.file is accepted as name without validation.
name reaches filesystem path arguments consumed by convert.

false_positives.why: A traversal sequence in the file query value can make the conversion process read from or write outside the intended upload and output directories.

false_positives.evidence: searchProducts sends database rows to the caller and contains no actor identity or authorization check.
false_positives.fix: Require authentication at route registration and enforce a server-side policy that filters or authorizes product records for the authenticated actor before responding.
false_positives.title: Product search returns records without an observable authorization decision

trace.note: The handler accepts caller-controlled search input without establishing an actor.
Database rows are returned to the caller without an authorization decision.

false_positives.why: If the exported handler is registered without omitted middleware, an unauthenticated caller can retrieve product search results contrary to the documented product-access rule.

false_positives.evidence: findProduct returns rows for req.params.id and contains no actor identity or authorization check.
false_positives.fix: Require authentication at route registration and enforce a server-side product-read policy for the authenticated actor before returning rows.
false_positives.title: Product lookup returns records without an observable authorization decision

trace.note: req.params.id is used to select records without an established actor.
Selected database rows are returned without an authorization decision.

false_positives.why: If the exported handler is registered without omitted middleware, a caller can retrieve a product by changing its identifier without a demonstrated product-access decision.
